sections.h2: How is South Fulton different from other places where owners sell a house?
sections.html:
South Fulton is a young city with an unusual setup: it took over zoning, police, fire and code enforcement in 2017, yet property valuation and tax billing still run through Fulton County. That split decides which office you call about each piece of a sale.

Georgia lawmakers passed the incorporation bill in 2016, and 59 percent of voters approved the charter that November. The city took effect on May 1, 2017. With it, Fulton County became the first county in Georgia with no unincorporated residential areas, and the county stopped providing municipal services such as fire, police and zoning.

The 2020 census counted 107,436 residents, which made South Fulton the state's eighth-largest city. It was carved from southwest Fulton County and takes in many older communities that kept their names. Confirm the tax district and zoning for your exact address before you sign anything.

sections.h2: Which communities make up South Fulton?
sections.html:
The city was assembled from existing southwest Fulton communities, and buyers and agents still describe houses by those names. The city's published community list includes:

  • Red Oak, Cooks Crossing and Stonewall
  • Fife, Ben Hill and Sandtown
  • Cliftondale, Ono and Cedar Grove
  • Boat Rock and Dry Pond, Maude and Lester
  • Enon, Welcome All and Peters Woods
  • Part of Campbellton

The Old National Highway corridor is the city's main commercial street. An announcement in 2023 set about 700 acres along the highway for a major revitalization that was scheduled for completion in 2028, so a seller near the corridor may find buyers asking about construction and future uses. Public parks add to the picture, with 17 parks on roughly 692 acres, including Burdett, Sandtown and Welcome All parks, plus the Wolf Creek Amphitheater with 5,420 seats.

Ask the city's zoning staff what the zoning district is for your lot, because that governs everything from fences to rentals.

sections.h2: Which schools serve South Fulton houses?
sections.html:
Fulton County Schools serves the entire city, and the city itself runs no school district. Most students attend schools in the Westlake cluster, which includes Westlake High, Camp Creek Middle, Sandtown Middle and elementary schools such as Seaborn Lee, A. Philip Randolph and Stonewall Tell. Some parts of the city feed other Fulton clusters, namely Banneker, Creekside and Langston Hughes.

Utilities, sanitation, elections and public health come from Fulton County or private providers rather than the city. When you give a buyer a list of what the house connects to, name the county or provider and not the city, so the buyer calls the right office at closing.

Attendance boundaries can change by street, so point buyers to the school system's own address lookup instead of promising a school assignment in the listing.

sections.h2: What permits does South Fulton require for repairs before a sale?
sections.html:
The city's Development Services division, part of Community Development and Regulatory Affairs, handles permits, and applications are filed through the SagesGov portal. Permit staff can be reached at 470-809-7200, extension 1, between 8:30 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.

The city's building permit page says the division processes these residential items:

  • New construction and demolitions
  • Alterations, additions and renovations
  • Sheds and fences
  • Retaining walls
  • Mechanical, electrical and plumbing trade permits

Inspections are scheduled in the same portal, and a request made before 4 p.m. can be conducted the next business day. State minimum construction codes were updated effective January 1, 2026, including the 2024 International Residential Code with Georgia amendments, so contractors should be working to the newer editions. If you plan only light repairs, call the permitting line before starting and ask whether the work needs a permit. Skipping that step can lead to trouble when a buyer's inspector or the city's code staff notices.

sections.h2: Can I sell a South Fulton house that I was renting out short term?
sections.html:
Yes, but the permit status should be clean before you list. In 2025 the city dropped its Special Use Permit requirement for short-term rentals and replaced it with a standard permit application. Short-term rentals are defined as lodging for no more than 30 consecutive days, and they are allowed only in residential zoning districts.

The application can be emailed or dropped off at City Hall. A non-refundable $200 application fee is invoiced after the city receives and approves the application at intake. Running a rental without a valid permit may bring fines, penalties or suspension, and repeated violations can lead to denial of later applications. The city also posts a running list of permit applications with a status of approved, denied or pending, and it accepts public comment on pending ones.

If a permit is pending or was denied, tell a buyer up front. Ask the city's community development staff whether a permit carries over to a new owner before you promise a buyer anything about future rental use.

sections.h2: How do South Fulton property taxes and appeals work when I sell?
sections.html:
The City of South Fulton states that its property taxes are billed and collected through the Fulton County Tax Commissioner, while the Board of Assessors sets value, accepts homestead applications and handles appeals. The county's 2026 notices of assessment showed estimated tax savings rather than an estimated tax bill, following a change in state law, and the appeal deadline for most owners was July 31, 2026.

An appeal must be filed within 45 days of the notice date, online, by mail or in person, and an appeal covers value only. Pick one of three routes when you file: a Board of Equalization hearing, non-binding arbitration, or a hearing officer, and note that some routes carry fees. While an appeal is pending you may receive a temporary bill that you must still pay.

Homestead applications filed after the April 1 deadline can be accepted during the appeal window for owners who held the home on January 1. The South Fulton Service Center for both the assessors and the tax commissioner is at 5600 Stonewall Tell Road. The assessors' phone line is 404-612-6440 and the tax commissioner's is 404-613-6100.

sections.h2: What should a South Fulton seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
Plan on a deed recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court of Fulton County and a transfer tax payment tied to that recording. The state tax department says questions about taxability and exemptions go to the clerk of the county where the property sits. Your closing attorney will also look for unpaid taxes and code liens, since both can delay a deed.

South Fulton short-term rental permit facts from the city's permit page
ItemWhat the city says
Permit typeStandard STR permit; Special Use Permit no longer required as of 2025
DefinitionLodging for a period not exceeding 30 consecutive days
Where allowedResidential zoning districts only
Application fee$200, non-refundable, invoiced after intake approval
Without a permitFines, penalties or suspension of rental activity

Sellers who want certainty often compare three paths: listing with an agent, selling as-is to an investor, or a direct cash sale. The right one depends on repairs needed, timing and how much net cash you need after liens and taxes.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a South Fulton house?
faqs.a: Fulton County does. The city says its taxes are billed and collected through the Fulton County Tax Commissioner.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my South Fulton assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date printed on the notice of assessment. After that deadline, your right to appeal that year's value is lost.

faqs.q: Do I need a Special Use Permit to run a short-term rental in South Fulton?
faqs.a: No. Since 2025 the city uses a standard STR permit with a $200 non-refundable application fee, and rentals are allowed only in residential zoning districts.

faqs.q: Can I fix up my house without a permit before selling?
faqs.a: Only for work the city does not regulate. Alterations, additions, renovations, sheds, fences and trade work such as electrical and plumbing go through the permitting division.

faqs.q: Which county office handles the deed when I sell?
faqs.a: The Clerk of Superior Court of Fulton County records the deed after the transfer tax is paid. The state tax department directs exemption questions to that clerk.
